profile.reading: Per DC BLOX own site, this Birmingham, Alabama facility sits at 433 6th Street South and currently operates 31,000 square feet, supporting up to 5 MW of critical load today and expandable to 60 MW; DC BLOX has published expansion plans totaling 263,000 square feet and 49 critical MW committed and planned for large scale deployments. The facility holds Uptime Institute Tier III Certification of Constructed Facility, meaning it is concurrently maintainable with no shutdowns required for equipment maintenance or replacement.

reading.body:
DC Blox's Birmingham facility publishes 5 MW of IT capacity today, making it the only data center in Alabama with a confirmed megawatt figure in available sources. This ranking reflects absence of published power data from other Alabama facilities rather than a verified market lead.

The facility operates 31,000 square feet under Uptime Institute Tier III Certification and can expand to 263,000 square feet and 49 MW through planned buildout. At standard colocation density of 10 kW per rack, 5 MW supports roughly 500 racks. At AI training density of 40 kW per rack, the same power envelope supports roughly 125 racks. The operator has not published per-rack power specifications, so current deployment type cannot be determined from this source.

Alabama remains a minor data center market by published capacity. The 5 MW represents the state total on record here, but many regional facilities do not publish power figures. Tenant information and workload specifics are not public. This data does not show whether the facility currently serves AI workloads or whether expansion plans target GPU-dense deployment. The gap between current capacity and expansion plans suggests infrastructure investment in the region, but does not indicate grid or real estate constraints that would distinguish Birmingham from other secondary markets.
